claims.behaviour: Migrate from backup: structure-field resolution of forest items runs once, when the backup's `structureFields` section has been read to its end. That section comes after `structures` and `histories`, so all forests are already saved, and it is read whichever option checkboxes were chosen. A backup without a `structureFields` section gets no resolution at all: a memo with `{"fields": {"duedate": "2026-01-05"}}` keeps those parameters word for word and no field problem is reported. Example: a backup whose memos use only plain text and date system fields has no `<field>` or `<value>` entries and therefore no such section.

Migrate from backup: resolution covers exactly the generic items this migration created, that is rows written as `item` with a `name` child (memos, planning tasks, any other type registered on this instance as a generic item type), including those found only in history forests, and including those with no `fields` parameter at all. Issues, projects, components, versions, folders, generators and effectors are not affected. Items of a backup structure that could not be saved (no new id) are skipped without a message: they stay as created, with no owning structure. An item whose type is unknown here was never created (see `Failed to create item <type>`) and is not resolved.

Migrate from backup: each key of an item's `fields` parameter is a backup field id, resolved one key at a time. First a field with that id is looked up on this instance. If the backup has no `<field>` entry for the id (it only writes entries for custom fields, so this is the case for all system fields such as `assignee`, `duedate`, `priority`, `project`, `issuetype`), the field found by id is used with no further comparison. Example: `fields` key `customfield_10010` with no `<field id="customfield_10010">` in the backup, and a field `customfield_10010` of any name and type here: that field is used.

Migrate from backup: when the backup has a `<field>` entry for the id and this instance has a field with the same id, that field is kept only if all three agree: the name (exact, case-sensitive, against the field's untranslated name), the type key (`fieldInfo` `type`, such as `single-line-text`) and the properties (the `rendererType` in the `<properties>` JSON; no `<properties>` matches a field with no renderer, and unreadable `<properties>` count as none). Example: backup `customfield_10010` named `Team`, type `single-line-text`, and here `customfield_10010` named `Team`, same type, no renderer on either side: the id is kept. Renamed to `team` here: not a match.

Migrate from backup: when the same-id check fails or no field has that id, and the backup has a `<field>` entry, the field is searched by the entry's name among all fields of this instance that the plugin supports, then narrowed to the same type key and equal properties. The value is then stored under the found field's id, and the old id disappears from the item. Example: backup `customfield_10010` `Team` (`single-line-text`); here `customfield_10010` is `Squad` and `customfield_10077` is `Team`, also `single-line-text`: `{"customfield_10010": "Red"}` becomes `{"customfield_10077": "Red"}`. A field of the same name but another type or renderer is not a match.

Migrate from backup: several fields here matching by name, type and properties is not an error and reports nothing: the first one in field order wins, where system fields come first (a system field's name for this comparison is its id) and custom fields follow in the order of `CustomFieldManager.getCustomFieldObjects()`. Example: `customfield_10077` and `customfield_10099`, both `Team` and `single-line-text`, listed in that order: the value goes to `customfield_10077` only.

Migrate from backup: a field that resolves to nothing is left out of the item, and the item's other fields are still resolved and stored. This covers: no field of that id and no `<field>` entry; a `<field>` entry with no match by name, even when a differently named field has the same id (no fallback to the id match); and a custom field here whose Jira type the plugin does not support, which is invisible to the search (a Sprint field when Jira Software is absent, for example). A problem is reported for the item's structure with i18n key `str.admin.restore.warning.generic-item.field-not-found`, for example `Found problems while resolving item com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo/7 fields: could not resolve a field from backup (ID customfield_10010)`, where the item is the new item id and the field the backup id. The migration goes on.

Migrate from backup: when the backup has no `<value>` entry for the resolved field's type key (always so for text, number, date, date-time, duration and label fields), the stored value is read with the resolved field's type and written back. Example: `{"customfield_10077": "Red"}` keeps `Red`. A value that type cannot read is dropped without any problem being reported: `abc` in a `single-number` field leaves that field out of the item, and only a log warning shows it.

Migrate from backup: for a single-valued option field whose type has `<value>` entries, the stored value S is looked up in the entries of that type key (shared by all fields of the type), and the resolution value R names the target: project key, issue type or priority name, version name, user name, group name, sprint name, or the custom field option's text. R is searched here without any security filter. Example: S `JIRAUSER10100` with R `anna`, and user `anna` here has key `JIRAUSER20200`: the item stores `JIRAUSER20200`. If S has no entry or nothing here has that name, the field is cleared from the item, the other fields are kept, and a problem is reported: `Found problems while resolving item <id> fields:Field <field name> value (<R, or S when unmapped>) isn't allowed by the project configuration` (there is no space after `fields:`; the two i18n texts are `str.admin.restore.warning.generic-item` and `s.ext.type.memo.error.misconfigured-field`; the field name is the untranslated one, for a system field its id).

Migrate from backup: for a multi-valued option field (versions, components, multi user, multi group, multi option) the stored JSON list is taken element by element. An element with no `<value>` entry is skipped silently. An element whose R names nothing here is left out and reported; the elements found stay, in order. Example: `["101","102","103"]` with 101 mapped to `1.0`, 102 mapped to `2.0` and 103 unmapped, and only `1.0` existing here: the item keeps the new id of `1.0`, and one problem is reported, `Found problems while resolving item <id> fields:Field fixVersions value ([2.0]) isn't allowed by the project configuration`. When nothing is left, the field is removed from the item.

Migrate from backup: name lookup of a value is not limited to the item's project, and several candidates give no problem: the first one Jira returns is used. Example: version `1.0` exists in projects A and B and the planning task's project is B: the version Jira lists first for the name `1.0` is stored, even if it is A's. Version and component names must match exactly (a component search that ignores case is narrowed to the exact text). A custom field option is searched among the options of the found field's configuration for no project and no issue type, so an option that exists only in a project-specific context is not found and is reported as in the single- and multi-valued cases.

Migrate from backup: before any field of a planning task (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-planning-task`) is looked at, its backup `project` and `issuetype` field values are turned into a project key and an issue type name through the `<value>` entries of types `single-project` and `single-issue-type`. The project must exist here by key, then the issue type by exact name among all issue types (not only the project's). On failure, in this order, a problem is reported and no field of the item is changed: unknown key `Found problems while resolving item <id> fields:Project ABC not found`; no key `...fields:Project is required`; unknown name `...fields:Issue type Bug not found`; no name `...fields:Issue type is required`. The item keeps all of its backup `fields`, so ids from the other instance stay in it. A planning task with no `fields` at all gets `Project is required`. Other item types skip this check.

Migrate from backup: during field resolution every found field counts as visible, editable and not required, for every item type, whatever the target project's field configuration says. Example: a memo with a custom field keeps it even though a memo's normal editing shows only its fixed field set, and a planning task missing a field that is required in the target project gets no problem.

Migrate from backup: after all fields of an item are resolved, the option values are checked once more, this time as the user running the migration, so a project, version or component that user cannot see fails. On a failure the item is not updated at all: it keeps the parameters it was created with (backup ids included), and one problem is reported with the text `Found problems while resolving item <id> fields:; <exception text>`, where the exception is a `StructureException` of `StructureErrors.UPDATE_ITEM_FAILED` carrying the field's message (`s.ext.type.memo.error.misconfigured-field`). When several fields fail, only one of them is reported, and which one is not defined. Other items continue.

Migrate from backup: after resolution the item's `fields` parameter holds only the resolved fields; all other parameters stay, and a parameter with a null value is removed. If nothing is left, `fields` is removed. A `summary` or `description` key among the fields sets the item's name or description instead of staying in `fields`. Because `fields` is rebuilt from nothing, the usual estimate rule applies: an item with a non-blank `timeoriginalestimate` and a blank `timeestimate` also gets `timeestimate` with the same value, and the other way round. Example: `{"fields": {"timeoriginalestimate": "7200"}}` comes out as `{"fields": {"timeoriginalestimate": "7200", "timeestimate": "7200"}}`.

Migrate from backup: every item that went through resolution without a validation failure, even with nothing to change, is saved through `GenericItemManager.updateItem` with the new structure id as owning structure, which adds one change record (old and new item, the current user, the current time) after the creation record, and marks the item as changed. Together with `migrateGenericItemHistory`, items that have records in the backup then lose those local records in favour of the backup's. An item that no longer exists when its turn comes is skipped silently.

Migrate from backup: a generic item that appears in two migrated structures is created once and queued for the first structure that named it. The second structure to be saved gets its own copy of the item, made from the item as it was then, and that copy is never resolved: it keeps the backup's field ids and values and reports nothing (as the original does).

Migrate from backup, with `migrateGenericItemHistory`: the old and new item of each `historyRecord` in the backup go through the same resolution (old only when `oldName` is not blank), with the same problems reported, each distinct text once. A validation failure drops that one record and reports `Found problems while restoring generic item history record for item <new id>; <exception text>`, once per distinct text, after the section ends. A record whose item was not resolved adds the general problem `A generic item for history mapping is not found`, and one with a blank `newName` adds `An updated item is not found in history record`; both are dropped. Records of a structure not read successfully are dropped with only a log line.

Migrate from backup: the old and new items stored in a migrated generic-item history record carry the backup's structure id as owning structure, not the new one, while the item itself carries the new id. Example: backup structure 5 migrated to 12: the item's owning structure is 12, its history snapshots say 5 (as the original does).

Migrate from backup: field problems never fail the migration: the result is still `Structure Migration Completed Successfully`, under the warnings text. A structure that has only field problems is listed among the invalid structures, with its name and new id, and its problems follow its other problems, HTML-encoded, in the order first found, with identical texts shown once. `ErrorsContainer.getStructureFieldResolutionProblems()` holds them per structure in that order, and `getInvalidStructures()` includes those structures.

Migrate from backup: forest items' field problems are recorded under the structure's new id, but the result page's list converts every key from backup id to new id once more. So when a new id equals the backup id of another migrated structure, the problems appear under that other structure. Example: backup 5 becomes 7 and backup 7 becomes 9: a problem of an item now in structure 7 is listed under 9 (as the original does).

Migrate from backup: problems from generic-item history are recorded under the backup structure id and those of forest items under the new id. When the two differ and a structure has both, the conversion for the result page gives both the same key, and one set replaces the other instead of being merged, so only one set is listed; which one depends on hash order and is not defined (as the original does).

The migrate options page does not try field resolution: reading the backup for the preview checks no field and gives no warning about fields that will not resolve. They show up only on the result page.

Restore (`RestoreOperation`, the restore page) uses the same field matching, value mapping, planning task check, validation and problem texts as migrate, and it runs at the same moment, at the end of the `structureFields` section, with the same result when there is no such section. Restoring a backup onto an instance whose custom field ids differ therefore moves values to the field of the same name, type and properties, as in migrate.

Restore differs from migrate in these ways. Items keep their backup id and get their owning structure when created, so nothing depends on structure ids changing. Only items with a non-empty `fields` map are resolved: an item without fields is not touched, gets no extra change record, and a planning task with no fields gets no `Project is required` problem. Items of all structures met in the file are resolved, even of a structure that failed to save, and an item that could not be restored is skipped silently. Problems are recorded under the backup structure id, which is also the id on the result page, with no second conversion, so the wrong-structure and lost-problems cases of migrate cannot happen.

A backup file that the current reader refuses and that the restore page then reads with the older format reader gets no field resolution: `structureFields` and generic-item history sections in it are ignored, with no problem reported.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/update`: an `add` with a blank `forest` whose `under`, `after` or `before` is a transient row id, sent with a `version` whose signature differs from the source's current one, does not give the signature-mismatch reply. Working out the first row of the empty fragment throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`, nothing catches it, and the request answers 500, `text/plain`, with the exception's message as body (`Index 0 out of bounds for length 0` on Java 11 and later), plus an error in the server log. There is no `forest-update-response`, so no `updateError`, no `forestUpdates` and no resynchronization of the client (as the original does). Example: `{"spec": {"structureId": 1}, "version": {"signature": 1, "version": 5}, "actions": [{"action": "add", "forest": "", "under": 7}]}` with current signature 2. The same happens for a `copy` with a blank `forest` and `originalRowIds: []`.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/update`: when an empty-fragment action ends the request with a 500, the action itself changes nothing, and its `cutFrom` removal (tried only as a dry run so far) has not happened, nor is the clipboard cleared. Actions earlier in the same request stay applied, with their effects, but the 500 reports nothing about them: no `successfulActions`, no `forestUpdates`, no `effects`. The usage counter `updateForest` has been raised for the action, and `updateForest.errors` has not.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/update`: an `add` or `copy` with a blank `forest` on a structure's forest, when the signature check passes, is first checked as any other add: `under`, `after` or `before` missing from the forest gives 200 with `updateError.error`, `row` 0 and message `Row <id> is not in the forest.`, and a coordinate under the wrong parent gives `Row <id> is not under row <parent>.`; lack of edit permission is reported as usual. If all of that passes, it fails like the signature case: 500, `text/plain`, body `Index 0 out of bounds for length 0` on Java 11 and later, and nothing is changed, also with `dryRun` (as the original does). So on a structure an empty `add` never succeeds, even though the blank `forest` was accepted.

`POST /rest/structure/2.0/forest/update`: an `add` with a blank `forest` and no coordinates on the caller's clipboard forest succeeds and counts in `successfulActions`. It empties the clipboard, as any add there first clears it, and adds nothing, so `oldRowIds` and `newRowIds` stay absent; with `dryRun` the clipboard keeps its rows. With a transient coordinate and a changed signature the signature case still applies: 500, not the mismatch reply.
